title: Ideal operations in finite rings

problem.name: Ideal operations in finite rings
problem.statement_latex: Given a uniquely encoded finite black-box ring $R$, generators of ideals $I,J$, and $a\in R$, compute an additive basis of an ideal, decide $a\in I$, or compute generators of $I\cap J$ and annihilators as specified in the paper. Complexity counts reversible ring operations and gates.
problem.statement_text: Given a uniquely encoded finite black-box ring $R$, generators of ideals $I,J$, and $a\in R$, compute an additive basis of an ideal, decide $a\in I$, or compute generators of $I\cap J$ and annihilators as specified in the paper. Complexity counts reversible ring operations and gates.

quantum.headline_latex: $\operatorname{poly}(\log|R|)$ time by Wocjan--Jordan--Ahmadi--Brennan, using uniform ideal states and abelian hidden-subgroup computations.
quantum.headline_text: $\operatorname{poly}(\log|R|)$ time by Wocjan–Jordan–Ahmadi–Brennan, using uniform ideal states and abelian hidden-subgroup computations.

classical.headline_latex: Once an additive basis and multiplication constants are available, Smith-normal-form and finite-module algorithms run in polynomial bit complexity. For a generic black-box input, constructing the needed coordinates has the $\widetilde O(|R|^{1/2})$ generic-group bound.
